quests.instruction: Where should you wait for a bus to come and pick you up?
quests.hint: It is a marked spot at the side of the road, often with a sign or a shelter.
quests.explanation: A bus stop is where buses pull in to let passengers on and off. Waiting there keeps you safe and tells the driver where to stop.
quests.funFact: In many cities, bus stops have timetables or screens that show when the next bus will arrive.

quests.instruction: Where do you buy a ticket and wait on a platform for a train to arrive?
quests.hint: Trains line up beside long, raised areas where passengers stand.
quests.explanation: A railway station is where trains stop for people to get on and off. Platforms keep passengers beside the tracks, and signs help them find the right train.
quests.funFact: Grand Central Terminal in New York has 44 platforms, one of the largest numbers of any station.

quests.instruction: Where do cars stop to fill their tanks so they can keep driving?
quests.hint: Look for pumps with long hoses beside the road.
quests.explanation: A petrol station has pumps that put fuel into a vehicle's tank. Cars, trucks, and buses with engines need fuel to keep running.
quests.funFact: Electric vehicles do not use fuel pumps. They charge their batteries at special charging points.

quests.instruction: Which signal uses red, yellow, and green lights to tell drivers when to stop and go?
quests.hint: It hangs above or stands beside a busy crossroads and keeps changing colour.
quests.explanation: Traffic lights control the traffic at crossings. Red means stop, yellow means get ready to stop, and green means go when the way is clear.
quests.funFact: The first electric traffic light was installed in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1914.

quests.instruction: Which red sign with eight sides tells drivers they must stop completely?
quests.hint: Count its sides and look at its colour. It also has a short word on it.
quests.explanation: A stop sign means vehicles must come to a full stop and check the road before moving on. Its special shape helps drivers recognise it quickly.
quests.funFact: In many countries, the stop sign is the only road sign shaped like an octagon.

quests.instruction: Which barrier warns drivers that the road is being repaired or built ahead?
quests.hint: Look for the barrier that tells drivers the road is not ready for normal driving.
quests.explanation: Roadworks barriers and signs tell drivers to slow down and take care. They keep workers safe and show where the road is being mended.
quests.funFact: Many roadworks signs are bright orange or yellow because those colours are easy to see from far away.

quests.instruction: Who sits at the front of an airplane and steers it through the sky?
quests.hint: This job needs special training and lots of buttons to check before a flight.
quests.explanation: A pilot is trained to fly an airplane. Pilots check the controls, listen to instructions from the ground, and keep passengers safe in the air.
quests.funFact: Pilots and air traffic controllers talk by radio so planes stay a safe distance apart.

quests.instruction: Who rides on a fire engine and uses hoses and ladders at an emergency?
quests.hint: This helper wears a helmet and heavy protective clothes.
quests.explanation: A firefighter puts out fires and rescues people. The fire engine carries the water, hoses, and tools needed for the job.
quests.funFact: Firefighters also rescue people from floods and car crashes, not only fires.

quests.instruction: What do we call a person who travels on foot along the pavement?
quests.hint: No wheels, no boat, and no pedals. Only feet.
quests.explanation: A pedestrian is a person who walks. Pedestrians use pavements and crossings, and drivers must watch out for them.
quests.funFact: Walking is the oldest way of getting around, and it needs no vehicle at all.

quests.instruction: Which round part turns to help cars, buses, and bicycles roll along the ground?
quests.hint: Look for the part that actually touches the road.
quests.explanation: A wheel rolls, which makes moving heavy things much easier than dragging them. Most land vehicles rely on wheels.
quests.funFact: The first wheels were made of solid wood, long before spokes were invented.

quests.instruction: Which part stores electricity so an electric car can drive without a petrol engine?
quests.hint: Think of what powers a torch or a phone, only much bigger.
quests.explanation: An electric car uses a big battery to store electricity. The battery powers a motor that turns the wheels.
quests.funFact: Many electric cars can top up their batteries a little every time they slow down.

quests.instruction: Which heavy metal hook is dropped from a boat to stop it drifting away?
quests.hint: It sinks to the bottom and holds on tight.
quests.explanation: An anchor is lowered to the bottom of the water, where it grips the sea or river bed. This keeps the boat from floating away.
quests.funFact: The anchors on very large ships can weigh several tonnes.

quests.instruction: What do you often show at a station or gate before you can board a train or plane?
quests.hint: It can be a small piece of paper or a phone screen that proves you have paid.
quests.explanation: A ticket shows that you have paid for a journey and where you are going. Staff or machines check it before you travel.
quests.funFact: Many people now keep their tickets on their phones instead of on paper.

quests.instruction: What do travellers pack their clothes and belongings in for a long trip?
quests.hint: It has a handle and often rolls along on small wheels.
quests.explanation: A suitcase keeps your things together while you travel. Stations and airports have special places for luggage so it does not block the way.
quests.funFact: At airports, bags ride along moving conveyor belts to reach the right plane.

quests.instruction: What helps travellers see roads, rails, and places so they can plan a route?
quests.hint: It shows where things are, drawn as if seen from high above.
quests.explanation: A map shows roads, rail lines, rivers, and places. It helps travellers choose a route and know where to turn.
quests.funFact: Many phone maps update when roads get busy, so drivers can choose quicker routes.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle is smaller than a bus but has more seats than most cars?
quests.hint: Think of what a sports team or a big family might use.
quests.explanation: A minibus or van fits a group of people or lots of goods in one vehicle. It is handy when a car is too small but a bus is too big.
quests.funFact: Vans are used as delivery vehicles, ambulances, and even mobile shops.

quests.instruction: Which train glides along one single beam instead of two rails?
quests.hint: Look at what is beneath it. There is only one track.
quests.explanation: A monorail runs on a single rail or beam. Many are raised above the streets, so they carry people without adding to road traffic.
quests.funFact: Some monorails carry people around theme parks and between airport buildings.

quests.instruction: Which sleek train with a pointed nose is built to travel at very high speed?
quests.hint: Its smooth, pointed front helps it slip through the air.
quests.explanation: A high-speed train runs on special smooth tracks and has a streamlined front. It lets people travel between cities much faster.
quests.funFact: Japan's first bullet train began running in 1964.

quests.instruction: Which round ring can be thrown to someone in the water to help them float?
quests.hint: It floats, and a person can hold on to it until help arrives.
quests.explanation: A lifebuoy is a floating ring kept on boats and docks for emergencies. Throwing one to someone in the water helps them stay up until they can be rescued.
quests.funFact: Many harbours and boats keep lifebuoys in places where they can be grabbed quickly.

quests.instruction: Which structure is built high over a river so vehicles can cross without a boat?
quests.hint: Look for something built above the water, not beside it.
quests.explanation: A bridge carries a road or railway over a river, valley, or another road. It gives vehicles a way across places they could not drive through.
quests.funFact: Japan's Akashi Kaikyō Bridge is one of the longest suspension bridges in the world.

quests.instruction: What is made of two long metal rails that trains roll along?
quests.hint: A train's wheels fit exactly on top of it.
quests.explanation: A railway track holds trains on their path. The metal rails guide the wheels, and the sleepers underneath keep the rails in place.
quests.funFact: Railway tracks are usually laid on small stones, which help hold them steady.

quests.instruction: Which wide road is built for cars and trucks to travel quickly over long distances?
quests.hint: It has several lanes so vehicles can travel at higher speeds.
quests.explanation: A highway has multiple lanes and few junctions. It lets vehicles cover long distances faster than on small town streets.
quests.funFact: Many highways have a middle strip or barrier so traffic going in opposite directions stays apart.

quests.instruction: Which road sign warns drivers to slow down because children may be crossing nearby?
quests.hint: You often see it near schools and playgrounds.
quests.explanation: Children can be hard for drivers to see, so this sign reminds drivers to go slowly and carefully.
quests.funFact: Some schools have crossing patrols who hold up a sign to stop traffic so children can cross.

quests.instruction: Which blue sign shows a place where cars can wait while their drivers go inside?
quests.hint: The sign has just one big letter.
quests.explanation: A parking sign marks a place where vehicles can be left safely when they are not moving. Parking in marked spaces keeps roads clear for everyone.
quests.funFact: Some cities have multi-storey car parks with hundreds of spaces stacked on top of each other.

quests.instruction: Which small airplane with a propeller at the front carries only a few people on short flights?
quests.hint: It is far smaller than the airplanes you see at big airports.
quests.explanation: A light aircraft is small, with one or two propellers. It is used for pilot training, short trips, and reaching places without big airports.
quests.funFact: Some small planes can be fitted with floats or skis to land on water or snow.

quests.instruction: Which picture shows an airplane coming down to touch the runway?
quests.hint: The nose points downward, toward the ground.
quests.explanation: Landing is when a plane comes down from the sky and touches the runway. The pilot slows the plane and lowers its wheels as it gets close.
quests.funFact: Airplane wheels fold up inside the plane after take-off to help it fly more smoothly.

quests.instruction: Which low, very fast car is built to race around a track?
quests.hint: It is made to be light and to sit very close to the ground.
quests.explanation: A racing car has a powerful engine, a low body, and wide tyres that grip the track. It is built for speed, not for family trips.
quests.funFact: Racing cars have wings that push them down onto the track, the opposite of an airplane wing.

quests.instruction: Two of these ride on rails. Which one does not?
quests.hint: Look for the one with rubber tyres that drives on the road.
quests.explanation: Trams and subway trains follow rails. A bus has tyres and drives on the road, so it can change its route if the road is closed.
quests.funFact: Some buses are electric and run on batteries instead of petrol or diesel.

quests.instruction: Which one is the odd one out because it cannot float on water?
quests.hint: Think about which of these is built for fields, not for waves.
quests.explanation: Sailboats and ferries are made to float. A tractor is built for farmland and would sink in deep water.
quests.funFact: Big steel ships float because their hollow shape pushes aside a lot of water.

quests.instruction: Pilots fly two of these. Which one has to stay on the road?
quests.hint: Look for the one without wings or spinning blades.
quests.explanation: Airplanes and helicopters can leave the ground. A taxi stays on the road, with its wheels always touching the surface.
quests.funFact: Airplane wings are shaped so that moving air helps lift the plane upwards.
